name: South Korea (1945–1948)
description: A white field with a red and blue taegeuk in the centre surrounded by four black trigrams, drawn in the pre-1949 pattern with the trigrams arranged differently from the present flag.
history: Version of the Taegukgi used in the American-occupied south of Korea between the liberation of 1945 and the establishment of the Republic of Korea. The Constituent National Assembly adopted the Taegukgi as the national flag on 12 July 1948, and the National Flag Correction Committee fixed the present geometry on 15 October 1949.
